[size=4][b]THIS IS A TESTING VERSION. (85% passed.)[/b][/size]
[size=3]I've done some testing but I can't really test it as thoroughly as people making mods with it can. I looked around and couldn't find a scripting interface/mod for SMAPI. So I made one so more people can write mods. C# and build chains can be a scary barrier for people.[/size]

[size=4][b]NOTE:
[/b][/size][size=3]Mod loading and save loading taking an extra few seconds is normal. SMAPI scans included DLLs and IronPython has big ones. I tried moving them to a separate folder because the scanning is unnecessary. But that makes it crash when it can't trace the dependency. Saving/sleeping performance was unaffected. The default included example scripts bind the function keys and do basically [b]cheats[/b] for testing. I'm leaving them as examples. If you're concerned about accidently [b]cheating[/b] I would remove them before launching. But tbh having a scratch save for testing your mod is always a good idea. To be clear this mod is just basically duct taping Lua and Python interpreters to SMAPI's methods. It shouldn't corrupt saves etc. All gamestate touching unless using raw is through SMAPI.[/size]

[b][size=4]Description:[/size][/b]
[b]Stardew Script[/b] embeds pure managed [b]MoonSharp (Lua 5.2)[/b] and [b]IronPython 3 (Python 3.4+)[/b] runtimes directly into SMAPI. It lets you write mods in Python or Lua or mix both in the same mod with high-level API abstractions, shared state, and instant hot-reloading on script save. No C# compiler, Visual Studio setup, or game restarts required. Just save your script and watch it run live in-game.

[size=4][b]Installation:[/b][/size]
Install SMAPI (I built it against 4.5.2.)
Put the StardewLua folder in the usual mods folder.
It looks inside the scripts directory inside the StardewLua folder for the Lua/Python scripts.
Inside scripts there is a test/example main.lua and main.py. You can delete them or reference them.

[b][size=4]Main Features:[/size][/b]
[size=3][b]Near/Complete API Coverage:[/b] 925 methods and properties across 16 modules.[/size]
[b]Live Hot-Reloading:[/b] Background file watcher detects changes on file save and updates code in-game instantly.
[b]Lua and Python:[/b] Write in your preferred scripting language with identical API naming conventions.
[b]High-Level Game API:[/b] Clean hooks for player stats, inventory, NPCs/dialogue, locations, crops, audio, and custom 2D HUD/World batch drawing.
[b]Cross-Platform:[/b] Pure managed assemblies compatible with Windows, macOS, and Linux/Steam Deck.
(I specifically chose MoonSharp and IronPython because they are platform agnostic.)
[b]Markdown Docs:[/b] In the docs.zip there's some API documentation.
[b]Proxies: [/b]Proxy modules[b] [/b]for ease of use.
[b]Raw Mode (Lua/Python): [/b]Raw mode using reflection and type coercion for when you REALLY need to hook deeper into the engine/other mods.
[b]Multiplayer Script Sync:[/b] When you join, the host's scripts are sent to you and are loaded. Changes that the host makes to the scripts are also synced. (Let me know if the interpreter reloading causes any weird issues or missed edge cases.)
[b]Test Coverage:[/b] 85% (It's a massive surface to test. I'll be working through what wasn't covered by the test scripts.)

[b][size=4]Requirements:[/size][/b]
[b]SMAPI[/b] 4.0.0 API or newer. (I used 4.5.2.)
[b]Stardew Valley[/b] 1.6+
